title: Dedicated autoscaler: smoother burst control and utilization reporting improvement
author: Ethan Chen
description:
Motivation: customers running Dedicated fleets observed oscillation when transient traffic spikes caused token-bucket burst allocations to be exhausted and the autoscaler to rapidly scale up/down. This led to higher tail latency and noisy utilization reports. This PR smooths burst allocation behavior, improves utilization/queue reporting granularity, and adds observability to make regressions visible in the Console.

What this PR changes: 1) Autoscaler smoothing: introduce a leaky-bucket smoothing layer on top of the token-bucket burst allocator to gradually ramp burst allowance down instead of instant evaporation. This reduces reactive scaling spurts and prevents flux in short windows. 2) Burst budget rebalancing: allow per-fleet burst budgets to borrow from idle pools for short windows when global capacity exists, bounded by a safety cap. 3) New metrics: added dedicated.fleet.burst_utilization, dedicated.fleet.queue_length_percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and dedicated.fleet.effective_capacity to improve forensic and historical analysis. 4) Reporting pipeline: emit delta-based summaries to reduce cardinality noise and aggregate at 1-min and 5-min rollups. 5) Tests and docs: unit tests for smoothing logic, integration test exercising scale-down stabilization, console dashboard JSON and a changelog entry.

Implementation notes: - The smoothing layer is implemented in autoscaler/tokenbucket/smoother.go and is pluggable; the default config keeps behavior unchanged unless a smoothing window > 0 is configured. - Metrics are added as tags/labels compatible with our metrics migration (no new storage backends). Aggregation is handled in observability/rollups to avoid increasing ingest costs. - Borrowing logic exists behind a feature flag (feature.dedicated_burst_borrowing) and is disabled by default.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4123) - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Console dashboard JSON updated - [x] Feature flag gated borrowing behavior - [x] Backwards compatible metric names and rollups

Testing: ran unit tests locally and on CI (all passing after addressing a race in tokenbucket_test), ran dedicated e2e in our perf lab with synthetic spike scenarios showing 30% reduction in 95th latency and 18% fewer scale operations across test windows. Observability tests validate the new metrics are present and roll up correctly.

Rollout plan: - Stage rollout: enable smoothing window=20s by default for canary fleets, monitor dedicated.fleet.burst_utilization and queue percentiles. - If metrics show improvement at canary, incrementally roll to remaining fleets over 48 hours. - Burst borrowing remains off until follow-up AB test completes.

Backward compatibility: no breaking API changes. Metrics names are additive and feature-flag guarded where runtime behavior might differ.
